frameworks.name: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) - Revolutionary FAR Overhaul numbering
frameworks.description:
The governmentwide procurement regulation, rewritten and renumbered by the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO). The RFO returned the FAR to its statutory roots, rewrote it in plain language and removed most non-statutory rules. Per Army Warranting Program Policy v12 (MAR 2026), RFO numbering is in effect in FAR, DFARS and AFARS from 1 February 2026, so cite RFO numbers at the board and be ready to say what the old number was.
- Each part below links to its page in the RFO Part and Deviations Guide on acquisition.gov.
- Parts 20, 21, 38 and 51 are reserved; 38 and 51 were removed by the RFO and their surviving coverage moved into Part 8.
- Part 30 is overhauled but acquisition.gov flags its cost-impact coverage for later removal to the Cost Accounting Standards.

parts.title: Federal Acquisition Regulations System
parts.summary: Part 1 is the rulebook about the rulebook: who writes the FAR, how it is numbered, when an agency may deviate, and where a contracting officer's authority comes from. For a warrant board this is the part that matters most, because Subpart 1.4 carries KO authority, appointment and termination, and the ratification of unauthorized commitments. Under the RFO the old 1.602 and 1.603 material now lives at 1.402 and 1.403, and ratification moved from 1.602-3 to 1.405.

key_sections.title: Guiding principles - strategies not addressed in the FAR
key_sections.note: If it is not prohibited by law, regulation or the FAR, a KO may do it; the RFO put this permission principle up front.

key_sections.title: Individual deviations
key_sections.note: One-time deviation for a single contract action, approved at the level the FAR and agency supplement set.

key_sections.title: Class deviations
key_sections.note: How DoD issues the DFARS RFO class deviations you are working under today.

key_sections.title: Contracting officers - Authority
key_sections.note: Only a warranted KO may bind the Government, and only within the limits on the certificate of appointment.

key_sections.title: Contracting officers - Responsibilities
key_sections.note: The KO safeguards the Government's interest, ensures compliance, and requests specialist assistance.

key_sections.title: Selecting, appointing, and terminating the appointment for contracting officers
key_sections.note: The appointment framework the Army Warranting Program Policy implements; 1.403-1(b) is the cite in the Army policy for delegation of appointment authority.

key_sections.title: Ratification of unauthorized commitments
key_sections.note: Formerly 1.602-3. Know the criteria and that ratification is by an official above the KO, not by the KO who found the problem.

parts.title: Definitions of Words and Terms
parts.summary: Part 2 holds the governmentwide definitions, almost all of it in one section. Boards use it to pin down the dollar thresholds and the words that decide which authority applies - micro-purchase threshold, simplified acquisition threshold, commercial product, commercial service, and construction. When a definition moves, whole procedures move with it.

key_sections.title: Definitions
key_sections.note: Micro-purchase threshold, simplified acquisition threshold, commercial product and commercial service all live here.

key_sections.title: Definition of 'Construction'
key_sections.note: The RFO folded the old 36.102 construction definition into 2.101.

key_sections.title: Contract clause
key_sections.note: Prescribes the definitions clause carried into the contract.

parts.title: Improper Business Practices and Personal Conflicts of Interest
parts.summary: Part 3 is the integrity part: procurement integrity, gratuities, kickbacks, contingent fees, contractor ethics programs and whistleblower protection. A board will push here on what you do the moment you learn of a possible violation. The short answer is stop, document, notify counsel and the chain, and do not proceed until it is resolved.

key_sections.title: Standards of conduct
key_sections.note: Strict avoidance of any conflict of interest or even the appearance of one.

key_sections.title: Procurement integrity
key_sections.note: Bans disclosure of contractor bid or proposal information and source selection information; drives the post-employment and reporting rules.

key_sections.title: Contractor Gratuities to Government Personnel
key_sections.note: Applicability, the clause, reporting suspected violations and treatment of violations.

key_sections.title: Reporting suspected antitrust violations
key_sections.note: Identical bids and other bid-rigging indicators go to the Attorney General through counsel.

key_sections.title: Subcontractor kickbacks
key_sections.note: Anti-Kickback Act coverage and the KO's duty when kickbacks are suspected.

key_sections.title: Whistleblower Protections for Contractor Employees
key_sections.note: Policy, complaints, remedies, and the prohibition on confidentiality agreements that restrict reporting.

key_sections.title: Preventing Personal Conflicts of Interest
key_sections.note: Applies to contractor employees performing acquisition functions closely associated with inherently governmental functions.

parts.title: Administrative and Information Matters
parts.summary: Part 4 covers the paperwork that proves the deal: contract files, unique identifiers, SAM registration, signatures, reporting and closeout. The RFO restructured it into presolicitation, solicitation/award and postaward subparts and pulled contract-file content from the old 4.8 up to 4.101. Boards ask what has to be in the file and how long records are kept.

key_sections.title: Contract files
key_sections.note: The RFO home of the old 4.801-4.803: the file must tell the complete story of the acquisition to a reader who was not there.

key_sections.title: System for Award Management
key_sections.note: Registration is a condition of award; check exclusions before you sign.

key_sections.title: Contracting officer's signature
key_sections.note: Only the warranted KO signs, and the certificate limits govern.

key_sections.title: Contract reporting
key_sections.note: Action reporting into the federal award data system.

key_sections.title: Contract closeout
key_sections.note: Closeout responsibility and timelines; a standing board topic for administration warrants.

key_sections.title: Contractor Records Retention
key_sections.note: Policy, how retention periods are calculated, and the specific periods.

parts.title: Publicizing Contract Actions
parts.summary: Part 5 tells you what must be publicized, where, and for how long, so industry gets a fair shot. Under the RFO the old 5.2 presolicitation material is at 5.101 and the solicitation notice content is at 5.201. A board will test the link between failing to synopsize and a sustained protest.

key_sections.title: Policy
key_sections.note: Publicize to increase competition, broaden industry participation and support small business.

key_sections.title: Presolicitation notice
key_sections.note: RFO home of the old 5.202 exemptions from the synopsis requirement.

key_sections.title: Special notices
key_sections.note: Industry days, sources sought, long-range acquisition estimates.

key_sections.title: Solicitation notice - Content
key_sections.note: RFO home of the old 5.102(a)(6) content requirement.

key_sections.title: Synopses of contract awards - General
key_sections.note: When an award notice is required.

key_sections.title: Announcement of contract awards
key_sections.note: Public announcement thresholds and the congressional notification rhythm.

parts.title: Competition Requirements
parts.summary: Part 6 is the competition part and one of the two or three most heavily tested at a CORB. The RFO renumbered every exception: the old 6.302 series is now 6.103-1 through 6.103-7, and the justification and approval rules moved from 6.303/6.304 to 6.104. Be able to name your exception, cite it in RFO numbering, and state who approves at your dollar value.

key_sections.title: Full and open competition
key_sections.note: The default: all responsible sources permitted to compete.

key_sections.title: Set-asides for small business concerns
key_sections.note: Set-asides are a form of full and open competition after excluding sources, not an exception to competition.

key_sections.title: Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements
key_sections.note: Formerly 6.302-1. The brand-name justification authority; 6.103-1(d) covers brand-name descriptions.

key_sections.title: Unusual and compelling urgency
key_sections.note: Formerly 6.302-2. Limit the period to the minimum needed and still request offers from as many sources as practicable.

key_sections.title: International agreement
key_sections.note: Formerly 6.302-4. The authority most often raised in Korea for SOFA and international agreement driven actions.

key_sections.title: Authorized or required by statute
key_sections.note: Formerly 6.302-5. Covers 8(a) sole source and other statutory authorities.

key_sections.title: Justification and approval
key_sections.note: Formerly 6.303/6.304. 6.104-1 is content, 6.104-2 is the approval table; DFARS 206.104-71 sets the DoD tiers.

key_sections.title: Availability of the justification
key_sections.note: Post the J&A after award; urgency actions have their own posting rule.

parts.title: Acquisition Planning
parts.summary: Part 7 requires you to plan the acquisition before you solicit it, and to document that plan. The RFO consolidated the plan requirements at 7.102 and renumbered the consolidation and bundling rules into 7.107-2 through 7.107-4. Boards ask who writes the plan, who approves it, and what triggers bundling analysis.

key_sections.title: Acquisition plans - Requirements
key_sections.note: RFO consolidation of the old 7.102-2; plan for the whole acquisition, not just the award.

key_sections.title: Agency-head responsibilities
key_sections.note: Where agency supplements such as AFARS 5107.103-90 hook in.

key_sections.title: General procedures
key_sections.note: Start planning as soon as the need is identified; involve the requiring activity, small business and counsel.

key_sections.title: Consolidation, bundling, or substantial bundling - Policy
key_sections.note: Absorbed the old 7.107-3 and 7.107-4; requires market research and a written determination.

key_sections.title: Consolidation and bundling - Notifications
key_sections.note: Formerly 7.107-5; notice to industry and to SBA.

key_sections.title: Inherently governmental functions - Policy
key_sections.note: You may not contract out an inherently governmental function; a frequent services board question.

parts.title: Required Sources of Supplies and Services
parts.summary: Part 8 sets the priority order for where you buy before you go to the open market - mandatory sources, AbilityOne, Federal Prison Industries, and the Federal Supply Schedules. With FAR Part 38 now reserved, the schedules material sits in Subpart 8.4. A board expects you to check required sources first and to document why you did not use them.

key_sections.title: Mandatory sources for specific supplies and services
key_sections.note: The required-source hierarchy you work through before open-market buying.

key_sections.title: Acquisition From AbilityOne Participating Nonprofit Agencies
key_sections.note: Mandatory source for listed products and services.

key_sections.title: Acquisitions From Federal Prison Industries, Inc.
key_sections.note: Market research decides comparability; exclusion rules at 8.302.

key_sections.title: Federal Supply Schedules - General
key_sections.note: Schedule ordering procedures; the RFO folded old Part 38 coverage into Part 8.

key_sections.title: Use of existing contracts
key_sections.note: Look for an existing vehicle before starting a new one.

key_sections.title: Contractor use of Government supply sources
key_sections.note: When a contractor may or must be authorized to use Government sources.

parts.title: Contractor Qualifications
parts.summary: Part 9 is responsibility, debarment and suspension, and organizational conflicts of interest. The section numbers survived the RFO largely intact, which makes this a clean citation to give a board. Expect to be asked how you make an affirmative responsibility determination and what you do when SAM shows an active exclusion.

key_sections.title: Policy
key_sections.note: Award only to a responsible prospective contractor; no award if you cannot make the affirmative determination.

key_sections.title: Standards
key_sections.note: The responsibility standards; 9.104-1 is the general standards - financial resources, schedule, performance record, integrity, facilities.

key_sections.title: Procedures
key_sections.note: How you obtain and document the information supporting the determination.

key_sections.title: Exclusions in the System for Award Management
key_sections.note: Check SAM exclusions before solicitation, before award, and before option exercise.

key_sections.title: Effect of listing
key_sections.note: No new awards to an excluded contractor absent a compelling-reason determination; 9.405-1 covers current contracts.

key_sections.title: Debarment
key_sections.note: Grounds and procedures; debarment is a business decision, not punishment.

key_sections.title: Organizational and consultant conflicts of interest - Applicability
key_sections.note: Unequal access to information, biased ground rules, impaired objectivity.

key_sections.title: Contracting officer responsibilities (OCI)
key_sections.note: Identify, evaluate, and avoid, neutralize or mitigate OCI as early as possible.

parts.title: Market Research
parts.summary: Part 10 shrank dramatically in the RFO - it is now essentially a single requirement section. You must do market research appropriate to the circumstances before developing a new requirement and before soliciting above the simplified acquisition threshold. Boards use Part 10 to test whether a sole-source justification was really supported.

key_sections.title: Market research requirements
key_sections.note: When research is required, what it must be scaled to, and how the results drive the acquisition strategy.

key_sections.title: Clause
key_sections.note: The market research related clause prescription.

key_sections.title: Scope of part
key_sections.note: Applies to supplies and services, commercial and noncommercial, including set-aside and brand-name decisions.

parts.title: Describing Agency Needs
parts.summary: Part 11 governs how a requirement is written so that it invites competition rather than locking it out. The old 11.104 brand-name rule is now 11.204. Boards pair this with Part 6: an over-restrictive specification is a competition problem before it is a protest problem.

key_sections.title: Policy
key_sections.note: State needs in functional or performance terms so the maximum number of sources can compete.

key_sections.title: Voluntary consensus standards
key_sections.note: Use existing standards rather than writing agency-unique ones.

key_sections.title: Items peculiar to one manufacturer
key_sections.note: Formerly 11.104. The brand-name or equal rule that pairs with FAR 6.103-1(d) and DFARS 211.204.

key_sections.title: Liquidated Damages
key_sections.note: Policy, procedures and clauses when delay damages are hard to estimate.

key_sections.title: Priorities and Allocations
key_sections.note: DPAS rated orders - routine for OCONUS support requirements.

parts.title: Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services
parts.summary: Part 12 is the commercial part and the RFO expanded its role: the old FAR 13.5 simplified procedures for commercial items now live at 12.201-1 with a $9 million ceiling, and contract type moved from 12.207 to 12.104. Commercial terminations are still at 12.304 and are settled by agreement, not by Part 49 procedures. For a Class II warrant, know the 12.102 restriction rule and the SaP ceiling cold.

key_sections.title: Preference
key_sections.note: Preference for commercial products and services and for commercial components.

key_sections.title: Restricting competition
key_sections.note: You may not restrict competition to a commercial brand without a justification under Part 6.

key_sections.title: Contract type
key_sections.note: Formerly 12.207. Firm-fixed-price or fixed-price with EPA is the norm; T&M and labor-hour need a determination.

key_sections.title: Simplified procedures (commercial, up to $9 million)
key_sections.note: RFO home of the old FAR 13.5 authority; 12.201-1(b) carries the old 13.004 rule on the legal effect of quotations.

key_sections.title: Combined synopsis/solicitation
key_sections.note: Formerly 12.603; one notice serves as synopsis and solicitation.

key_sections.title: Solicitation provisions and contract clauses
key_sections.note: Formerly 12.301; the 52.212 family tailored for commercial buys.

key_sections.title: Terminations (commercial)
key_sections.note: Commercial terminations settle under the commercial clause, not the Part 49 settlement machinery.

key_sections.title: Micro-purchases
key_sections.note: General rules, purchase guidelines and methods for commercial micro-purchases.

parts.title: Simplified Procedures for Noncommercial Acquisitions
parts.summary: Part 13 was renamed and narrowed by the RFO: it now covers simplified procedures for noncommercial acquisitions, while the commercial simplified procedures moved to 12.201-1. Competition at 13.101 replaces the old 13.106-1, and purchase order clauses moved from 13.302-5 to 13.204. Micro-purchases sit in Subpart 13.4.

key_sections.title: Applicability
key_sections.note: Simplified procedures below the simplified acquisition threshold for noncommercial buys.

key_sections.title: Competition - soliciting from a single source
key_sections.note: Formerly 13.106-1(b); the documentation you owe when you solicit only one source.

key_sections.title: Small business
key_sections.note: The set-aside expectation inside simplified procedures.

key_sections.title: Procedures
key_sections.note: Solicitation, evaluation and award mechanics under simplified procedures.

key_sections.title: Contract clauses
key_sections.note: Formerly 13.302-5; the clauses that go into a noncommercial purchase order.

key_sections.title: Cancellations and terminations
key_sections.note: How you unwind a simplified acquisition.

key_sections.title: Micro-purchases - General
key_sections.note: Micro-purchase rules including the threshold definition at 2.101.

parts.title: Sealed Bidding
parts.summary: Part 14 keeps sealed bidding intact but reorganized into presolicitation, evaluation and award, and postaward. Award goes to the responsible bidder whose responsive bid is lowest, with no discussions. The mistakes rules - before and after award - are the classic board question.

key_sections.title: Preparation of invitations for bids
key_sections.note: IFB content and the uniform contract format at 14.202.

key_sections.title: Two-step sealed bidding
key_sections.note: When you need technical proposals first but still want to award on price.

key_sections.title: Bid opening
key_sections.note: Public opening, recording, and the point at which prices become public.

key_sections.title: Mistakes in bids
key_sections.note: Apparent clerical mistakes, and the verification you owe before award.

key_sections.title: Rejection of individual bids - materially unbalanced
key_sections.note: Formerly 14.404-2(g); unbalanced pricing that poses unacceptable risk is rejected.

key_sections.title: Award
key_sections.note: Lowest responsive, responsible bidder; 14.308 handles equal low bids.

key_sections.title: Mistakes after award
key_sections.note: The limited relief available once the contract is signed.

parts.title: Contracting by Negotiation
parts.summary: Part 15 was renumbered end to end by the RFO and is the part most likely to trip a candidate on citations. Source selection responsibilities moved from 15.303 to 15.201, evaluation factors from 15.304 to 15.104, the tradeoff and LPTA approaches from 15.101-1/-2 to 15.103-1/-2, and the source selection decision from 15.308 to 15.205. Pricing moved too: price analysis is now 15.404-1 under 15.404, certified cost or pricing data is 15.403-3, and price negotiation is 15.407.

key_sections.title: Early exchanges with industry
key_sections.note: Formerly 15.201(c); exchanges before receipt of proposals are encouraged.

key_sections.title: Developing a competitive source selection approach
key_sections.note: Formerly 15.101; 15.103-1 tradeoff and 15.103-2 LPTA.

key_sections.title: Establishing competitive evaluation factors and significant subfactors
key_sections.note: Formerly 15.304; price or cost must always be evaluated.

key_sections.title: Source selection responsibilities
key_sections.note: Formerly 15.303; the SSA's role and the KO's role as contracting officer.

key_sections.title: Competitive award with negotiation
key_sections.note: Formerly 15.306; exchanges, competitive range, and meaningful discussions.

key_sections.title: Source selection decision
key_sections.note: Formerly 15.308; the SSA's independent judgment, documented with rationale.

key_sections.title: Certified cost or pricing data
key_sections.note: Formerly 15.403-4; the TINA threshold and required actions. DoD's threshold is set by class deviation.

key_sections.title: Price analysis
key_sections.note: Formerly 15.404-1(b) under 15.404; the techniques for determining a fair and reasonable price.

parts.title: Types of Contracts
parts.summary: Part 16 is contract type selection and the indefinite-delivery family. The RFO moved multiple-award ordering procedures from 16.505 to 16.507, put the exceptions to fair opportunity at 16.507-6(b), and created a standalone 16.508 for protests of orders. Boards want the risk logic: who bears cost risk under each type and what you must document to justify anything other than firm-fixed-price.

key_sections.title: Policies
key_sections.note: Contract type is a risk allocation decision driven by uncertainty in requirements and pricing.

key_sections.title: Documenting contract type
key_sections.note: The written justification for the type selected.

key_sections.title: Firm-fixed-price contracts
key_sections.note: The default type; contractor bears full cost risk.

key_sections.title: Cost-reimbursement contracts - General
key_sections.note: Requires an adequate accounting system and appropriate Government surveillance.

key_sections.title: Indefinite-quantity contracts
key_sections.note: Guaranteed minimum, stated maximum, and the fair opportunity obligation.

key_sections.title: Additional ordering procedures for multiple-award contracts
key_sections.note: Formerly 16.505; 16.507-6(b) carries the exceptions to fair opportunity.

key_sections.title: Protests of orders
key_sections.note: Order protest jurisdiction; DoD's floor is set by statute and class deviation.

key_sections.title: Time-and-materials contracts
key_sections.note: Least preferred; requires a determination that no other type is suitable.

parts.title: Special Contracting Methods
parts.summary: Part 17 holds multiyear contracting, options, interagency acquisitions, management and operating contracts and reverse auctions. Options are the board favorite: 17.204-1 now carries the exercise rules that used to sit at 17.207, and the conditions at 17.204-1(b) are what you must satisfy before you sign the modification. Interagency business-case analysis is at 17.502-1(b).

key_sections.title: Multiyear Contracting
key_sections.note: Authority, presolicitation, evaluation and award, and the cancellation ceiling mechanics.

key_sections.title: Options - Presolicitation
key_sections.note: Options must be evaluated at solicitation to be exercised later.

key_sections.title: Options - Evaluation and award
key_sections.note: Evaluating option prices as part of award.

key_sections.title: Exercise of options
key_sections.note: Formerly 17.207. 17.204-1(b) sets the conditions: funds available, need continues, exercise is the most advantageous method, and the contractor is not excluded.

key_sections.title: Interagency acquisitions - Business-case analysis
key_sections.note: Required business case for multi-agency and governmentwide vehicles.

key_sections.title: Interagency acquisitions - Ordering procedures
key_sections.note: Economy Act and non-Economy Act determinations.

key_sections.title: Reverse Auctions
key_sections.note: When a reverse auction is and is not an appropriate technique.

parts.title: Emergency Acquisitions
parts.summary: Part 18 is now a single pointer section listing the flexibilities that become available in an emergency, contingency or declared disaster. It does not create authority on its own; it indexes authorities that live in other parts. Know that contingency designations raise the micro-purchase and simplified acquisition thresholds under FAR 2.101.

key_sections.title: Emergency acquisitions
key_sections.note: Formerly Subpart 18.2; the consolidated list of emergency flexibilities and where each one is codified.

key_sections.title: Scope of part
key_sections.note: Part 18 identifies flexibilities; the underlying authority stays in its home part.

key_sections.title: Contingency and emergency threshold definitions
key_sections.note: Contingency, humanitarian and disaster designations raise the MPT and SAT; confirm current values before you rely on them.

parts.title: Small Business
parts.summary: Part 19 was renumbered heavily: the whole socioeconomic program set now sits inside Subpart 19.1 as sections 19.104 through 19.109. The rule of two moved from 19.502-2 to 19.104-1, HUBZone from 19.13 to 19.105, SDVOSB from 19.14 to 19.106, WOSB from 19.15 to 19.107, 8(a) from 19.8 to 19.108, and subcontracting plans from 19.7 to 19.109. Expect to be asked the rule of two and who your small business professional is.

key_sections.note: Formerly Subpart 19.4; working with SBA and the procurement center representative.

key_sections.title: Small business size standards
key_sections.note: Formerly 19.102; NAICS code drives the size standard.

key_sections.title: Total small business set-asides (rule of two)
key_sections.note: Formerly 19.502-2. Reasonable expectation of two or more responsible small businesses and award at a fair market price.

key_sections.title: HUBZone Program
key_sections.note: Formerly Subpart 19.13; 19.110 carries the price evaluation preference.

key_sections.title: Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Program
key_sections.note: Formerly Subpart 19.14.

key_sections.title: Women-Owned Small Business Program
key_sections.note: Formerly Subpart 19.15.

key_sections.title: Contracting With the Small Business Administration (the 8(a) Program)
key_sections.note: Formerly Subpart 19.8; 19.108-7 carries the competitive and sole-source 8(a) thresholds.

key_sections.title: Small business subcontracting plans
key_sections.note: Formerly Subpart 19.7; when a plan is required and what it must contain.

OCONUS candidates should know which of these follow the contract overseas and which do not. The construction wage determination timing rule moved from 22.404-6(c) to 22.403.

frameworks.name: Army Warranting Program Policy v12 (MAR 2026)
frameworks.description:
The ODASA(P) policy that governs Army warrants for Contracting Officers, Grants Officers and Agreements Officers. Version 12 reorganized the document into eight sections, simplified Table 1, moved Class I to the SAT and made SaP the top fixed threshold of Class II, and added the statement that FAR, DFARS and AFARS references implement the RFO and the DFARS RFO class deviations effective 1 February 2026.
- This is the document a CORB is run under. Know Table 1, how instrument value is calculated, and the board composition.
- The policy and the review board question repository live on the PAM Army Warranting Program page, which is CAC-gated.
- Sections below follow the v12 numbering.

parts.title: Purpose
parts.summary: Section 1 states what the policy covers - the standardized Army warranting program for Contracting Officers under the FAR, Grants Officers under 2 CFR 1108, and Agreements Officers under 32 CFR 3.4 - and where warrant authority comes from. ASA(ALT) designated procurement authority to DASA(P), who delegates selection, appointment and termination of KOs under FAR 1.403-1(b) and of GOs and AOs under 32 CFR 21.425. DASA(P) delegates warrant granting authority to the HCA.

key_sections.title: Authority
key_sections.note: A warrant is signatory authority to enter into, obligate, administer, terminate and sign related documents; 'warrant' and 'appointment' are used interchangeably.

key_sections.title: Delegation for KOs and AOs
key_sections.note: The HCA appoints KO and AO warrants and may delegate down to the SCO and no lower than the Chief of the Contracting Office.

key_sections.title: Delegation for GOs
key_sections.note: The HCA appoints GO warrants directly and shall not delegate that authority further.

key_sections.title: Selection and appointment authority
key_sections.note: The FAR cite the Army policy implements for KO appointment.

parts.title: Applicability
parts.summary: Section 2 says who the program covers - Department of the Army civilians, military personnel and Foreign Local Nationals who need a warrant under Army authority - and confirms the regulatory baseline. It states that FAR, DFARS and AFARS references in the policy implement the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul and the DFARS RFO class deviations effective 1 February 2026. It also names DoDGARs at 32 CFR Chapter I Subchapter C for grants and agreements, and the OT statutes.

key_sections.title: Statutory and regulatory compliance
key_sections.note: RFO and DFARS RFO class deviations effective 1 Feb 2026; DoDGARs at 32 CFR Chapter I Subchapter C; OTA at 10 U.S.C. 2808a, 4021, 4022 and 33 U.S.C. 2313.

key_sections.title: Warranting process
key_sections.note: The HCA ensures the organization's selection and warranting process aligns with mission requirements and is shared with the organization.

key_sections.title: Certificate of Appointment and letter
key_sections.note: The certificate states the limits on authority; the accompanying letter details responsibilities, expectations and the consequences of non-compliance, up to termination of employment.

key_sections.title: Additional information
key_sections.note: Points to the Army Warranting Program page on Procurement.Army.mil.

parts.title: Qualification Requirements
parts.summary: Section 3 covers candidate readiness, desirable characteristics, waivers and the qualification requirements for KOs, GOs and AOs. A KO warrant above the SAT requires the 10 U.S.C. 1724 and DFARS 201.403 requirements and an AT&L-designated position. Waivers are an HCA decision documented with a risk assessment and business case, must comply with 10 U.S.C. 1724(d) for KO qualification waivers, and must be in VCE-Warrants before the appointment.

key_sections.title: Candidate readiness
key_sections.note: Training, knowledge and experience to meet fiduciary responsibilities, plus any local requirements.

key_sections.title: Candidate characteristics
key_sections.note: Sound decision makers and critical thinkers who can interpret and apply statutes and regulations.

key_sections.title: Waivers
key_sections.note: HCA may waive qualification requirements including the review board, with written justification, risk assessment and business case, retained in VCE-Warrants.

key_sections.title: KO qualifications
key_sections.note: Above the SAT: 10 U.S.C. 1724, DFARS 201.403, and an AT&L designated position; below the SAT, the same training expectation.

key_sections.title: Foreign Local National KOs
key_sections.note: OCONUS HCAs may recognize equivalent education and training and must complete an FLN Validation Letter - directly relevant to 411th CSB in Korea.

key_sections.title: GO qualifications

key_sections.title: AO qualifications
key_sections.note: CON 0660 and CON 2880V or equivalent, OTA Credential preferred, data rights and intellectual property working knowledge, and a commensurate KO or GO warrant held or previously held.

parts.title: Standard Warrant Thresholds
parts.summary: Section 4 sets the fixed warrant value thresholds in Table 1 and how you calculate the value of the instrument you are signing. Class I is the SAT; Class II is $500K, $1M, $5M and SaP; Class III is $10M, $25M, $50M and $100M; Class IV is $250M, $500M and Unlimited. Because the certificate can name SAT and SaP rather than a dollar figure, a change in those statutory values does not force reappointment.

key_sections.title: Warrant thresholds classification
key_sections.note: Class I = SAT; Class II = $500K, $1M, $5M, SaP; Class III = $10M, $25M, $50M, $100M; Class IV = $250M, $500M, Unlimited.

key_sections.title: Calculating instrument value
key_sections.note: Your warrant must be greater than or equal to the cumulative instrument value: base plus all options plus anticipated or actual ceiling plus the absolute value of the modification, regardless of when funds are obligated.

key_sections.title: Unlimited warrants
key_sections.note: Passing the appropriate review board is mandatory for an unlimited warrant and cannot be waived.

key_sections.title: Multiple warrants
key_sections.note: An individual may hold KO, GO and AO warrants but must meet each set of qualifications; HCAs shall not issue the same warrant type twice to split pre-award and post-award limits.

key_sections.title: Legacy warrants
key_sections.note: No re-testing or re-boarding to keep a current warrant, including increases within the same class; moving to a higher class requires a new test or board and reappointment.

parts.title: Warranting Review Boards
parts.summary: Section 5 is the board itself. A candidate must pass the review board for the warrant type - CORB for contracting officers, GORB for grants officers, AORB for agreements officers - or have a previously passed board of the same type recognized by the current organization. The HCA chairs the board and selects three to five additional members mixing experience, legal expertise and supervisory background.

key_sections.title: Purpose and composition of the board
key_sections.note: The HCA chairs and administers; three to five additional members with experience, legal and supervisory backgrounds appropriate to the warrant type.

key_sections.title: Questions
key_sections.note: Questions are commensurate with the threshold, the candidate's role, the organization's mission, FAR and non-FAR instruments, and the level of responsibility; the PAM page holds a question and answer repository to customize from.

key_sections.title: Board recognition alternative
key_sections.note: An organization may recognize a previously passed board for the same warrant type instead of re-boarding.

key_sections.title: Unlimited warrant board
key_sections.note: The board is mandatory and unwaivable for an unlimited warrant.

parts.title: Virtual Contracting Enterprise Warrants Module
parts.summary: Section 6 makes VCE-Warrants the official Army repository for all warrants and requires it to be used to initiate, store, route and document every warrant action. It sets records retention - six years from suspension or termination for completed warrants, and disposal of incomplete packages 18 months after submission - and prohibits storing PII in the system. It also states that VCE-Warrants cannot transfer an active warrant between HCA organizations.

key_sections.title: Official repository
key_sections.note: VCE-Warrants at vce.army.mil/warrants is the official Army repository for all warrants.

key_sections.title: Records retention
key_sections.note: Certificate, approval memo and all supporting documentation are retained in VCE-Warrants; do not store PII.

key_sections.note: Organization/Office - fiscal year - sequence number, auto-generated or assigned manually.

key_sections.title: Records disposition
key_sections.note: Completed warrants: six years from suspension or termination. Incomplete packages: dispose 18 months after submission, absent written rationale for longer.

key_sections.title: Transferring warrants
key_sections.note: VCE-Warrants does not support transferring an active warrant between HCA organizations; an HCA may reinstate a warrant from another HCA organization.

parts.title: Suspension, Termination, or Reinstatement of Warrants
parts.summary: Section 7 lists the grounds for suspending and terminating a warrant and how each is documented. Suspension reasons include extended TDY, a performance improvement plan, investigation of the warranted officer's actions, and deployment or contingency support. Termination is required when the individual leaves employment or moves to a non-acquisition position, retroactive terminations are prohibited, and reinstating a terminated warrant requires a new Certificate of Appointment and letter.

key_sections.title: Suspension
key_sections.note: Extended TDY, performance improvement plan, investigation of KO/AO/GO actions, or deployment and contingency support; documented and retained in VCE-Warrants.

key_sections.title: Termination
key_sections.note: Required on departure or reassignment out of acquisition; grounds include mission change, unsatisfactory performance or misconduct such as Anti-Deficiency Act violations, fraud or negligence, loss of clearance, and exceeding delegated authority. Retroactive terminations are prohibited.

key_sections.title: Reinstatement
key_sections.note: The HCA may reinstate a suspended warrant; reinstating a terminated warrant requires a new Certificate of Appointment and letter, documented in VCE-Warrants.

parts.title: ACC Contracting Note 26-03 - ACC's Warrant Reciprocity Guidance
parts.summary: Issued 12 May 2026 and effective immediately, this Contracting Note tells the ACC workforce how warrant reciprocity works after the PAE restructure left warranted personnel under the operational control of Senior Contracting Officials outside their permanent organization. All SCOs must honor active and future warrants issued within ACC, and personnel operating under reciprocity do not need a new warrant. The Note states it does not establish new policy and is self-deleting when it becomes obsolete; the formal process lives in the ACC Acquisition Instruction at 1.403.

key_sections.title: Mandatory recognition within ACC
key_sections.note: Effective immediately, all SCOs are required to honor all active and future warrants issued within ACC; no new warrant is required to operate under reciprocity.

key_sections.title: Value on recognition or transfer
key_sections.note: Warrants are recognized or transferred at their existing dollar value; increasing the value requires standard warrant increase procedures, which may include a new review board. The ADCON organization processes increases unless the individual has permanently transferred, in which case the gaining SCO does.

key_sections.title: Recognition versus transfer
key_sections.note: Recognition is formal acceptance of an existing warrant by a different SCO while the warrant stays issued by the original SCO. Transfer is permanent movement of the warrant, which VCE-Warrants cannot do - so it means terminating the original warrant and issuing a new one under the gaining SCO.

key_sections.title: When reciprocity applies
key_sections.note: Multiple SCOs within one ACC organization, organizational realignments under one or more ACC organizations, and personnel under the OPCON of an SCO other than the issuing SCO.

key_sections.title: Internal transfers within ACC
key_sections.note: Transfer only on permanent reassignment between ACC organizations. The individual downloads the complete digital record from VCE-Warrants for the gaining organization; the gaining SCO issues the new warrant only after the previous one is terminated, and each file must be a complete standalone record.

key_sections.title: External warrants
key_sections.note: SCOs retain full discretion whether to formally recognize a warrant issued outside ACC, but a new ACC warrant must still be issued in VCE-Warrants. For Air Force arrivals, see the Army's Warrant Reciprocity MOA.

key_sections.title: Reinstating inactive warrants
key_sections.note: If a previous warrant was terminated in good standing, the SCO may recognize it and issue a new warrant of the same type and value; a new warrant must be issued in VCE-Warrants because the individual arrives without an active one.

key_sections.title: Systems guidance
key_sections.note: ACWS access is added by DoDAAC role in PIEE, PADDS by manually adding DoDAACs to the profile, and PCF by granting access to the specific organizations and cabinets.

thresholds.name: Micro-purchase threshold (MPT)
thresholds.applies: standard
thresholds.cite: RFO FAR 2.101 (definition of micro-purchase threshold); 41 U.S.C. 1902
thresholds.notes: Read on acquisition.gov FAR 2.101 (page header FAC 2026-01, effective 03/13/2026) and confirmed retained in the RFO Part 2 model deviation text at https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-2. Raised from $10,000 by FAR Case 2024-001 (FAC 2025-06, inflation adjustment) effective 1 Oct 2025. Carve-outs in the same definition: $2,000 for construction subject to wage-rate (Davis-Bacon) requirements; $2,500 for services subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute. Board angle: purchases at or below the MPT may be awarded without soliciting competitive quotations if the KO or appointed cardholder considers the price reasonable - RFO FAR 12.402(b) (RFO moved micro-purchase procedures to Subpart 12.4; RFO FAR 13.401(a) simply says 'Follow the procedure in 12.4'). Verified 13 Sep 2026 on the RFO Part 12 and Part 13 pages. DoD note: Class Deviation 2024-O0011 lets combatant commanders authorize higher MPTs for covered operations through 30 Sep 2028 (carried forward by DFARS Part 213 deviation 2026-O0029). Verifier 13 Sep 2026: $15,000 and the $2,000 / $2,500 carve-outs re-read on FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01) and the RFO Part 2 page; the 2024-O0011 carry-forward sentence re-read in DFARS deviation 2026-O0029 Attachment A1 (and repeated in the DFARS 212 deviation 2026-O0028).

thresholds.name: Micro-purchase threshold - contingency / CBRN defense / disaster / emergency, inside the United States
thresholds.applies: contingency (inside US)
thresholds.notes: Read verbatim on FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01). Applies to acquisitions that, as determined by the head of the agency, support a contingency operation; facilitate defense against or recovery from cyber, nuclear, biological, chemical or radiological attack; support international disaster assistance; or support an emergency or major disaster response. Legacy FAR 13.201(g) cite still resolves on acquisition.gov; RFO Part 13 section number for this paragraph was not confirmed. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: figure re-read verbatim on FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01, eff. 03/13/2026) and FAR 13.201(g).

thresholds.name: Micro-purchase threshold - contingency / CBRN defense / disaster / emergency, outside the United States
thresholds.applies: contingency (outside US)
thresholds.notes: FAR 13.201(g)(1)(ii) read verbatim: '$40,000 in the case of any contract to be awarded and performed, or purchase to be made, outside the United States.' Same triggering conditions as the $25,000 tier. Korea-relevant: applies only when the head of the agency has made the contingency/emergency determination - not a standing OCONUS figure. korea-verify-cp for any local implementation. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: figure re-read verbatim on FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01, eff. 03/13/2026) and FAR 13.201(g).

thresholds.name: Simplified acquisition threshold (SAT)
thresholds.applies: standard
thresholds.cite: RFO FAR 2.101 (definition of simplified acquisition threshold); 41 U.S.C. 134
thresholds.notes: Read on acquisition.gov FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01) and confirmed retained in the RFO Part 2 model deviation text. Raised from $250,000 by FAR Case 2024-001 (FAC 2025-06) effective 1 Oct 2025. Army Warranting Program Policy v12 Table 1: Class I warrant = SAT; the policy deliberately writes 'SAT' rather than a dollar figure so warrants need not be reissued when the value changes. Board angle: SAT drives Part 13 simplified procedures, the automatic small business reservation, synopsis/notice rules, the Service of Protest provision, and 10 U.S.C. 1724 KO qualification requirements above SAT. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: figure re-read verbatim on FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01, eff. 03/13/2026) and the RFO Part 2 model deviation page.

thresholds.name: Simplified acquisition threshold - contingency / CBRN defense / disaster / emergency, inside the United States
thresholds.applies: contingency (inside US)
thresholds.notes: Read verbatim on FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01): '$1 million' for contracts awarded and performed, or purchases made, inside the United States when the head of the agency determines the acquisition supports a contingency operation, CBRN attack defense/recovery, international disaster assistance, or emergency/major disaster response. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: figure re-read verbatim on FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01, eff. 03/13/2026) and the RFO Part 2 model deviation page.

thresholds.name: Simplified acquisition threshold - contingency / CBRN defense / disaster / emergency, outside the United States
thresholds.applies: contingency (outside US)
thresholds.notes: Read verbatim on FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01): '$2 million' for contracts awarded and performed, or purchases made, outside the United States under the same triggering determination. Korea-relevant only when a contingency/emergency determination is in effect; korea-verify-cp. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: figure re-read verbatim on FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01, eff. 03/13/2026) and the RFO Part 2 model deviation page.

thresholds.name: Simplified acquisition threshold - humanitarian or peacekeeping operation, outside the United States
thresholds.applies: humanitarian or peacekeeping operation (outside US)
thresholds.notes: Read on FAR 2.101 (FAC 2026-01): '$650,000' for any contract to be awarded and performed, or purchase to be made, outside the United States in support of a humanitarian or peacekeeping operation. Included because boards sometimes ask for every SAT tier; distinguish it from the $2 million contingency tier. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: '$650,000' re-read on FAR 2.101. Caution on the statutory cite: 10 U.S.C. 3015 as read at law.cornell.edu is titled 'Simplified acquisition threshold', defines 'humanitarian or peacekeeping operation', and expresses the outside-US figure as 'two times the amount specified in section 134 of title 41' rather than a dollar figure - the FAR 2.101 $650,000 figure (an inflation-adjusted 41 U.S.C. 153 value) is the one a KO applies; do not quote 10 U.S.C. 3015 for the dollar amount.

thresholds.name: Simplified procedures for commercial products and commercial services ceiling ('SaP' / legacy FAR 13.5 authority)
thresholds.applies: standard (commercial products/services above the SAT)
thresholds.notes: Two sources agree: legacy FAR 13.500 on acquisition.gov (FAC 2026-01) reads 'greater than the simplified acquisition threshold but not exceeding $9 million ($15 million for acquisitions as described in 13.500(c))'; the RFO Part 12 model deviation text (updated 20 Apr 2026) reads 'For acquisitions valued up to $9 million, issue a request for quotations (RFQ) followed by a purchase order' (12.201-1) with the ceiling stated in 12.001(c). IMPORTANT RFO CROSSWALK: the RFO moved commercial simplified procedures out of Part 13 into Part 12; RFO Part 13 is 'Simplified Procedures for Noncommercial Acquisitions' only (confirmed on the RFO Part 13 page and in DFARS Class Deviation 2026-O0029). Army Warranting Program Policy v12 Table 1 uses 'SaP' (Simplified Procedures - Commercial Products and Commercial Services) as the top Class II warrant value so warrants track this figure automatically. Raised from $7.5 million by FAR Case 2024-001 effective 1 Oct 2025. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: re-read on the RFO Part 12 page (last updated 07/28/2026): 12.001(c) 'The $9 million ceiling for the use of simplified procedures (see 12.201-1) is increased to $15 million if the head of the agency determines...'; 12.201-1(a) 'For acquisitions valued up to $9 million, issue a request for quotations (RFQ) followed by a purchase order'; 12.201-2 covers acquisitions greater than $9 million; the 12.102(b) authority table shows '> SAT, <= $9 million' and '> $9 million, <= $15 million'. Legacy 13.500(a) re-read. Note: the RFO Part 12 page date is 28 Jul 2026, not 20 Apr 2026.

thresholds.name: Simplified procedures for commercial products/services ceiling - contingency / CBRN defense / disaster / emergency
thresholds.applies: contingency (head-of-agency determination; inside or outside US)
thresholds.cite: RFO FAR 12.001(c) (legacy FAR 13.500(c)); 41 U.S.C. 1903
thresholds.notes: RFO Part 12 text: 'The $9 million ceiling for the use of simplified procedures (see 12.201-1) is increased to $15 million if the head of the agency determines that the supplies or services are to be used to' support a contingency operation, CBRN defense/recovery, international disaster assistance, or emergency/major disaster response. Legacy 13.500(c) page shows the same figure. Raised from $13 million (legacy) by FAR Case 2024-001. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: 12.001(c) sentence and legacy 13.500(c) re-read verbatim.

thresholds.name: Certified cost or pricing data (TINA / Truthful Cost or Pricing Data) threshold - DoD prime contracts awarded after 30 June 2026
thresholds.applies: DoD (prime contracts awarded after 30 Jun 2026; modifications use the same criteria as the prime)
thresholds.cite: 10 U.S.C. 3702(a)(1) as amended by FY2026 NDAA (Pub. L. 119-60) sec. 1804; DFARS 215.403-3(a) per DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048, Rev. 1 (22 Jul 2026)
thresholds.notes: Deviation text extracted from the PDF: '215.403-3 Certified cost or pricing data. (a) Threshold. In lieu of the requirements of FAR 15.403-3(a), obtain certified cost or pricing data when a prime contract is expected to exceed $10 million and is awarded after June 30, 2026, unless an exception at FAR 15.403-2 or 215.403-71 applies. The threshold is $2.5 million when the prime contract is awarded on or before June 30, 2026, unless otherwise stated in the contract (10 U.S.C. 3702).' Statute confirmed at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/10/3702 ('in the case of a prime contract entered into after June 30, 2026 ... expected to exceed $10,000,000'). The deviation memo says it implements NDAA FY2026 sections 811(a)(5), 812(c) and 1826; the $10M change itself is NDAA sec. 1804 per statute notes and trade press (governmentcontractslaw.com and insidegovernmentcontracts.com returned HTTP 403 so those were not read directly). Board answer: for an Army KO today the DoD threshold is $10 million; cite the statute and the DFARS deviation, and note the FAR text still says $2.5 million. Subcontract flow-down figures in the same deviation still show $2.5 million in places - read 215.403-3(a)(2) before quoting a subcontract number. The deviation index is at https://www.acq.osd.mil/dpap/dars/dfars_far_overhaul_class_deviations.html. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: deviation PDF re-downloaded and text re-extracted - 215.403-3(a) wording confirmed exactly, including '(2) ... subcontract ... (i) After June 30, 2026, and the price of the subcontract is expected to exceed $10 million'. Statute re-read at law.cornell.edu: 10 U.S.C. 3702(a)(1)(A) '$10,000,000' for prime contracts entered into after June 30, 2026, (a)(1)(B) '$2,000,000' on or before that date (the $2.5 million in the deviation is the inflation-adjusted figure), amendment note 'Pub. L. 119-60, div. A, title XVIII, sec. 1804(c)(1)(B)', enacted 18 Dec 2025. Memo's reference to NDAA sections 811(a)(5), 812(c) and 1826(8)-(9) confirmed.

thresholds.name: Certified cost or pricing data threshold - governmentwide FAR (civilian agencies; DoD prime contracts awarded on or before 30 Jun 2026)
thresholds.applies: standard (governmentwide FAR; DoD only for prime contracts awarded on or before 30 Jun 2026)
thresholds.notes: Value verified verbatim on legacy FAR 15.403-4 (FAC 2026-01): 'The threshold for obtaining certified cost or pricing data is $950,000 for prime contracts awarded before July 1, 2018, and $2.5 million for prime contracts awarded on or after July 1, 2018.' Raised from $2 million by FAR Case 2024-001 effective 1 Oct 2025. The RFO Part 15 page lists '15.403-3 Certified cost or pricing data' as the section heading (crosswalk 15.403-4 -> 15.403-3) but the fetch returned headings only, so the RFO section's body text was not read - hence 'probable'. Legacy 15.404-1 (price analysis) keeps the number 15.404-1 in the RFO. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: legacy 15.403-4(a)(1) '$2.5 million' re-read; the RFO Part 15 page again returned only the 15.403-3 heading (body not served), so the RFO section number stays 'probable'. Note the RFO renumbering makes 15.403-4 'Certificate of current cost or pricing data', so a board answer citing '15.403-4' for the threshold is now the wrong section under RFO.

thresholds.name: Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) contract-level applicability / exemption threshold
thresholds.applies: governmentwide (statute); contracts and subcontracts awarded on or after 1 Oct 2026 (before that: $2,500,000, TINA-linked)
thresholds.cite: 41 U.S.C. 1502(b)(1)(B) as amended by FY2026 NDAA (Pub. L. 119-60) sec. 1806; 48 CFR 9903.201-1(b)(2) as amended by CAS Board final rule 91 FR 56056 (1 Sep 2026, effective 1 Oct 2026); DFARS 230.201-70(b) per Class Deviation 2026-O0006 Rev. 1 (30 Jul 2026)
thresholds.notes: What was verified: (1) DoD deviation 2026-O0006 Rev. 1 text (PDF extracted) - 'the threshold for determining the tentative applicability of CAS at the contract level is the amount set forth in 41 U.S.C. 1502(b)(1)(B)' and the memo states it implements NDAA FY2026 sec. 1806; (2) acquisition.gov news item dated 2 Sep 2026 confirming the CAS Board published 'Increase of Monetary Thresholds and Other Matters Related to Cost Accounting Standards Program Requirements' at 91 FR 56056 on 1 Sep 2026. What was NOT read directly: the $35 million figure and the 1 Oct 2026 effective date come from web-search summaries of natlawreview.com, hunton.com, bmss.com, insidegovernmentcontracts.com and the Federal Register (federalregister.gov and ecfr.gov redirected to an unblock page; the CFR text at law.cornell.edu still shows the pre-rule 'TINA threshold, as adjusted for inflation' language and a $7.5 million (b)(7) trigger). Board answer as of 13 Sep 2026: the statutory exemption threshold is $35 million per the FY2026 NDAA; the CAS Board rule implementing it in 48 CFR 9903 is published and takes effect 1 Oct 2026; before that the regulation still ties the exemption to the TINA threshold. Confirm the effective-date wording in 91 FR 56056 before release. Verifier 13 Sep 2026 - PRIMARY SOURCES NOW READ: (1) Federal Register final rule 91 FR 56056-56060, document 2026-17901, published 1 Sep 2026, 'Effective October 1, 2026' (read via the FR API and the full-text .txt endpoint; the HTML page redirects to an unblock page). Amended 48 CFR 9903.201-1(b)(2) reads 'Negotiated contracts and subcontracts not in excess of $35 million. For purposes of this paragraph (b)(2), an order issued by one segment to another segment shall be treated as a subcontract.' (2) 41 U.S.C. 1502(b)(1)(B) at law.cornell.edu now reads 'in excess of $35,000,000, as adjusted in accordance with applicable requirements of law, including requirements relating to inflation in section 1908', amendment note Pub. L. 119-60 sec. 1806(d)(1)(A). (3) DoD deviation 2026-O0006 Rev. 1 230.201-70(b) re-read. Upgraded from probable to verified. Update 29 Oct 2026: the rule is now in force; the board answer is the single $35 million applicability threshold.

thresholds.name: CAS full coverage / Disclosure Statement threshold
thresholds.applies: DoD-only business units now (deviation); governmentwide from 1 Oct 2026 (CAS Board rule); legacy value $50,000,000
thresholds.cite: DFARS 230.201-70(a)(1) per Class Deviation 2026-O0006 Rev. 1 (30 Jul 2026), implementing FY2026 NDAA sec. 1806(a)(2); 48 CFR 9903.201-2(a) and 9903.202-1 as amended by 91 FR 56056 (effective 1 Oct 2026)
thresholds.notes: Deviation text extracted verbatim: 'full Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) coverage applies to contractor business units that have only DoD contracts and subcontracts and that (i) Receive a single CAS-covered contract award of $100 million or more; or (ii) Received CAS-covered contracts during its preceding cost accounting period with a net value of $100 million or more' and, for Disclosure Statement requirements, 'replace $50 million with $100 million wherever it appears'. Business units with mixed DoD and other federal work stay on FAR 30.201(b)/48 CFR 9903.201-2 ($50 million) until the CAS Board rule takes effect; the $100 million governmentwide figure and 1 Oct 2026 date are from secondary summaries (Federal Register not fetched). 48 CFR 9903.201-2 at law.cornell.edu still shows $50 million (last amended 76 FR 40819, 2011). Modified coverage (Disclosure and Consistency, 52.230-3): RFO FAR 30.205(b)(1) reads 'over $2.5 million but less than $50 million'; DoD deviation substitutes $100 million for $50 million. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: FR final rule 2026-17901 (91 FR 56056, effective 1 Oct 2026) read via the full-text endpoint: 9903.201-2 and 9903.202-1 are amended by 'Removing $50 million, wherever it appears, and adding, in its place, the text $100 million'; 9903.201-5(a) agency-head waiver authority raised from $15 million to $100 million. Deviation 2026-O0006 Rev. 1 230.201-70(a)(1) and (d)(1) text re-read from the PDF. Upgraded from probable to verified. RFO FAR 30.205(b)(1) still prints 'over $2.5 million but less than $50 million' (page last updated 07/28/2026) - expect a FAR Part 30 update after 1 Oct 2026.

thresholds.name: CAS $7.5 million 'trigger' exemption (business unit not performing any CAS-covered contract of $7.5M or more)
thresholds.applies: no longer in force: removed by 91 FR 56056 effective 1 Oct 2026; the single $35 million applicability threshold replaced it
thresholds.notes: Read verbatim at law.cornell.edu (current CFR text, last amended 83 FR 33148, 2018): 'Contracts or subcontracts of less than $7.5 million, provided that, at the time of award, the business unit of the contractor or subcontractor is not currently performing any CAS-covered contracts or subcontracts valued at $7.5 million or greater.' The 1 Sep 2026 CAS Board rule (91 FR 56056) raises the basic applicability threshold to $35 million, which makes this trigger largely moot; whether (b)(7) is retained, removed or re-set was not confirmed. Do not teach this figure without checking the final rule text. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: FR final rule 2026-17901 (91 FR 56056) read via the full-text endpoint: amendatory instruction 2 revises 9903.201-1(b) in full and adds (c); '$7.5 million' no longer appears anywhere in the amended 9903.201-1, and the preamble states 'The proposal also eliminated the $7.5 million trigger contract threshold as it would no longer be necessary with a higher applicability threshold.' Board answer: through 30 Sep 2026 the $7.5M trigger still exists in the CFR; from 1 Oct 2026 the single $35M applicability threshold replaces it. Upgraded from unverified to verified (as an eliminated legacy figure). One secondary read of the govinfo HTML suggested a paragraph (b)(7) survives under a different subject (NATO PHM ship program, currently (b)(6)) - the renumbered paragraph list was not itemized, so cite the rule, not a paragraph letter, after 1 Oct 2026. Update 29 Oct 2026: eliminated; keep only as history.

thresholds.name: Total small business set-aside - automatic reservation range
thresholds.value: Above the MPT ($15,000) - RFO FAR 19.104-1 sets no SAT ceiling on the set-aside requirement (legacy 19.502-2(a) band was MPT to SAT $350,000)
thresholds.applies: standard; mandatory in the United States and its outlying areas, discretionary outside (FAR 19.000(b))
thresholds.notes: REFUTED IN PART by verifier 13 Sep 2026. Legacy FAR 19.502-2 (FAC 2026-01) re-read verbatim and matches the original notes: (a) above the MPT but not over the SAT 'shall be set aside for small business unless' no reasonable expectation of two or more responsible small businesses competitive on fair market price, quality and delivery; (b) over the SAT, set aside when there is a reasonable expectation of at least two responsible small business offers and award at fair market prices. BUT the RFO text a KO must now use (RFO Part 19 page; DoD deviation 2026-O0037 Rev. 1 directs use of the RFO Part 19 'in lieu of the text codified at 48 CFR chapter 1') collapses the two tiers: 19.104-1(a) read verbatim - 'For contracts above the micro-purchase threshold, the contracting officer must set the contract aside for small business if there is a reasonable expectation of obtaining offers- (1) From two or more responsible small business concerns; and (2) That are competitive in terms of fair market prices, quality, and delivery.' 19.104-1(b)(1): 'The contracting officer must document the reason when a contract is not set aside for small business as required.' 19.104-1(c): the requirement 'does not apply to purchases at or below the micro-purchase threshold or purchases from required sources under part 8.' So under RFO numbering there is no MPT-to-SAT 'automatic reservation' band distinct from the over-SAT rule of two; the original value string described the legacy band only. Korea: FAR 19.000(b) re-read verbatim ('shall apply this part in the United States and its outlying areas' / 'may apply this part outside'), so Part 19 set-asides remain discretionary for 411th CSB awards in the ROK. Correction to the original note on DFARS 219: the Status-of-Forces-Agreement and 'both awarded and performed outside the United States' items in Class Deviation 2026-O0037 Rev. 1 are at 219.102-70(a)(4)-(5) and are exceptions to SBA procurement center representative REVIEW, not exemptions from set-asides. korea-verify-cp before stating any local 411th set-aside practice.

thresholds.name: Justification approval tiers - governmentwide FAR Table 6-1 (other than full and open competition / limited competition)
thresholds.value: $900,000 (KO certification) / >$900K-$20M (competition advocate) / >$20M-$90M (HCA; $150M for DoD, NASA, Coast Guard) / >$90M ($150M DoD) SPE
thresholds.applies: governmentwide FAR; superseded for DoD by DFARS 206.104-71 (see ja_dod_* items)
thresholds.cite: RFO FAR 6.104-2(b) Table 6-1 (legacy FAR 6.304); 41 U.S.C. 3304(e); 10 U.S.C. 3204(e)
thresholds.notes: Both the legacy FAR 6.304 page (FAC 2026-01) and the RFO Part 6 page (last updated 28 Jul 2026) show the same tiers: not exceeding $900,000 - the KO's certification at (RFO) 6.104-1(a)(12) serves as approval unless agency procedures set a higher level; over $900,000 to $20 million - competition advocate for the procuring activity (non-delegable); over $20 million to $90 million (or $150 million for DoD, NASA and the Coast Guard) - head of the procuring activity or a general/flag officer or GS-15-equivalent designee; over $90 million (or $150 million for DoD/NASA/Coast Guard) - senior procurement executive. Raised from $750K/$15M/$75M/$100M by FAR Case 2024-001. For an Army KO the operative table is the DoD one in DFARS 206.104-71 - see next items; commercial acquisitions over the SAT reach the same approvals through RFO FAR 12.102 ('prepare a written justification and obtain approval of the justification as described in 6.104'). Verifier 13 Sep 2026: RFO Part 6 page (last updated 07/28/2026) Table 6-1 re-read - rows '$900,000 or below', '>$900,000 - $20,000,000', '>$20,000,000 - $90,000,000 (>$20,000,000 - $150,000,000 for DoD, NASA, and the Coast Guard)', '>$90,000,000 (>$150,000,000 for DoD, NASA, and the Coast Guard)'; legacy 6.304 re-read with the same tiers. Note the RFO table's first row prints the certification reference as '6.104(a)(12)' while the justification-content list is at 6.104-1(a)(12) (the DFARS deviation cites 'FAR 6.104-1(a)(12)') - treat the RFO page text as a typo. L. 119-60, 18 Dec 2025, replacing $500,000 / $10,000,000 / $75,000,000), so even the DoD $150M rows in Table 6-1 are stale for DoD - use Table 206-1.

thresholds.name: Task/delivery order protest jurisdiction floor - DoD, NASA, Coast Guard (GAO exclusive)
thresholds.applies: DoD (orders under IDIQ contracts; protest permitted only at GAO, on any ground, when the order value exceeds this amount)
thresholds.cite: 10 U.S.C. 3406(f)(1)(B) as amended by FY2025 NDAA (Pub. L. 118-159) sec. 885(f), 23 Dec 2024; DFARS 252.216-7010(b)(1) per DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0045 Rev. 1 (15 Jul 2026); RFO FAR 16.508 (legacy FAR 16.505(a)(10))
thresholds.notes: Statute read at law.cornell.edu: 3406(f)(1)(B) 'a protest of an order valued in excess of $35,000,000', with the amendment note that Pub. L. 118-159 sec. 885(f) substituted $35,000,000 for $25,000,000. DoD deviation 2026-O0045 Rev. 1 (DFARS 216, PDF text extracted) carries the same figure in the clause: 'Within 10 days after the date a task order or delivery order is issued, where the value exceeds $35 million, and the protest is on the grounds that the order increases the scope, period, or maximum value of the contract under which the order is issued (10 U.S.C. 3406(f))'. Forum rule for the board: (1) an order protest on the ground that it increases the scope, period or maximum value of the contract may be heard by GAO or the Court of Federal Claims; (2) any other ground is heard ONLY by GAO and ONLY when the order value exceeds $35 million (3406(f)(2) gives GAO exclusive jurisdiction) - COFC has no jurisdiction over DoD task-order protests on other grounds regardless of value. RFO protest cites from the brief (33.104-3 agency, 33.105 GAO) were not re-verified here. Verifier 13 Sep 2026: statute re-read at law.cornell.edu - (f)(1)(B) '$35,000,000', amendment note '2024-Subsec. (f)(1)(B). Pub. L. 118-159 substituted $35,000,000 for $25,000,000', and (f)(2) 'the Comptroller General of the United States shall have exclusive jurisdiction of a protest authorized under paragraph (1)(B)'. The $35 million clause sentence is in DFARS clause 252.216-7010, Postaward Debriefings for Task Orders and Delivery Orders (OCT 2025), paragraph (b)(1), prescribed at 216.505-70 - the deviation does not restate FAR 16.508 itself. Legacy FAR 16.505(a)(10)(i)(B)(2) re-read: still '$25 million' for DoD, NASA and the Coast Guard (stale). RFO Part 16 page: the '16.508 Protests of orders' heading is the last item served and no body text follows it, so the RFO section body remains unread. thresholds.name: Prompt Payment - standard payment period and current interest-penalty rate
thresholds.value: 30 days after receipt of a proper invoice (or acceptance); interest rate 4.75% per year for 1 Jul - 31 Dec 2026
thresholds.applies: standard (value_number is the Treasury rate in percent, not a dollar threshold)
thresholds.cite: RFO FAR 32.907 and 5 CFR 1315 (OMB Prompt Payment rule); 31 U.S.C. 3902-3903; rate also used for CDA interest under 41 U.S.C. 7109
thresholds.notes: Rate read verbatim on the Bureau of the Fiscal Service page: 'The Prompt Payment interest rate for July 1 - December 31, 2026 is 4.75%.' (Federal Register notice 2026-13903 of 9 Jul 2026 was not fetchable - redirect to an unblock page.) FAR 32.907 on acquisition.gov (FAC 2026-01): paragraph (e) reads 'The Government will compute interest penalties in accordance with OMB prompt payment regulations at 5 CFR Part 1315'; (a) makes the interest penalty automatic 'without request from the contractor'; the 'more than 30 days after the designated billing office receives a proper invoice' wording at (a)(5) is specific to interim payments on cost-reimbursement service contracts - the general 30-day due-date rule is in 32.904 / 5 CFR 1315.4; the RFO Part 32 page keeps the number 32.907 under Subpart 32.9 but its body text was not returned. Board answer: the due date is 30 days after the later of receipt of a proper invoice or acceptance (7-day constructive acceptance), the rate is set by Treasury every six months, interest is automatic without a contractor request, and the same rate applies to CDA claim interest. thresholds.name: Statutory acquisition-related threshold inflation adjustment cycle
thresholds.value: Every 5 years (last: 1 Oct 2025 via FAR Case 2024-001 / FAC 2025-06; next: October 2030)
thresholds.applies: governmentwide (value_number is the year of the next scheduled adjustment)
thresholds.notes: FAR 1.109 (FAC 2026-01, effective 03/13/2026) read: the FAR Council adjusts statutory acquisition-related thresholds for inflation 'every 5 years, starting in October 2005, using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U)'; the matrix for the latest adjustment is in FAR Case 2024-001 on regulations.gov. Thresholds FAR 1.109 says are NOT escalated under 41 U.S.C. 1908: those set by 40 U.S.C. chapter 31 (Davis-Bacon $2,000), 41 U.S.C. chapter 67 (SCLS $2,500) and the Trade Agreements Act figures set by USTR. Separately, the CDA certification $100,000 and the task-order protest floors ($10M / $35M) were not changed by FAR Case 2024-001 - an observation from the current FAR/statute text, not a statement in 1.109. FAR 1.109 also notes (NDAA FY2018 sec. 821) that adjusted thresholds apply throughout the remaining term of a contract regardless of award date. Useful board answer to 'why did the SAT change?'.

updates.title: Where the FAR overhaul stands
updates.text: The RFO numbering has governed FAR, DFARS and AFARS practice since 1 February 2026 through class deviations (Army Warranting Program Policy v12). Formal rulemaking is under way: the FAR Council published its first proposed rules on 23 June 2026 (20 parts) and a second batch on 18 September 2026 (Parts 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 27, 28, 35, 36, 38, 44, 47 and 51 with their Part 52 clauses; comments closed 19 October 2026). No final rule had been published by 29 October 2026, so the deviation text still governs and the citations in this app stand. Part 19 (small business) is expected in a later batch.
updates.source: acquisition.gov/far-overhaul (page updated 26 Oct 2026); the Federal Register notices as reported by Wiley Rein, Nextgov and Washington Technology, September 2026. Secondary reports: confirm against the Federal Register before quoting a date in the board.

updates.title: Army preference for competition in the 8(a) program
updates.text: An ASA(ALT) memorandum signed by the Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army (Procurement) on 7 April 2026 directs Army contracting activities to use competitive procedures as the preference over 8(a) sole source to the maximum extent practicable.
